items.title: Senators’ Nick Cousins out at least a week after Chychrun hit
items.summary: Cousins exited Tuesday night’s game after taking a huge hit from the Capitals defender.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn A notable update after a massive collision on Tuesday night. When speaking to the media on Wednesday, Ottawa Senators head coach Travis Green revealed that forward Nick Cousins will miss at least a week to 10 days after taking a huge hit from Washington Capitals defenseman Jakob Chychrun. The play that put Cousins on the shelf came late in the third period at Canadian Tire Center. Cousins was looking to break the puck out of the Ottawa zone, but was leveled by Chychrun, who was pinching in from the left point. The hit sent Cousins soaring into the glass before falling flat to the ice. Cousins was left motionless on the ice before receiving assistance from the Senators’ training staff. He was taken off the ice and immediately brought to the team’s dressing room. He didn’t return to the game. No penalty was called on the play. Green confirmed what many who saw the hit believed, and that was the fact that Cousins was knocked out on the ice after the check. Tuesday night’s contest was Cousin’s 19th appearance of the 2026-27 season. The veteran center has struggled to find his offensive touch, scoring just two goals and three points thus far. He has a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 9:45 of ice time, amassing 44 penalty minutes. The Senators wrap up their quick home swing on Thursday night, hosting the Colorado Avalanche. Ottawa (11-6-2) sits fourth in the Atlantic Division, holding the first Wild Card spot in the Eastern Conference.

items.title: Canadian government official confirms visa denial of Russian players for 2027 World Juniors
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney previously stated that Russians wouldn’t be playing in the upcoming tournament.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Canada is digging in its heels about allowing Russia to play in Alberta next month. According to TSN’s Gord Miller, the Canadian government has told both Hockey Canada and the International Ice Hockey Federation it will not issue visas to Russian players seeking to play in the upcoming IIHF World Junior Championship. Also, players who might already have visas – players in the Canadian Hockey League – are considered ineligible to participate, even if it was under a neutral flag. This comes not long after Canadian prime minister Mark Carney stated that Russia “will not” be at the World Juniors, which are set to begin on Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer. The whole debate on whether Russia would be allowed to play in the upcoming event came after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation must be allowed to compete in IIHF events, citing that the IIHF didn’t provide enough evidence to keep the ban on Russian teams in place. The IIHF, along with numerous international hockey federations, has voiced its displeasure on the decision. Nations have come forward, stating that they won’t play Russia in any international events, with some big-time sponsors threatening to pull their funding from the IIHF, if Russia is allowed to compete. As it stands, Norway, the last-ranked team heading into the WJC, has been informed that it will be removed from the tournament to make way for Russia . However, many expect Russia to be forced to back out, leading to Norway’s readmission to the event. The ban on Russian hockey teams dates back to 2022, when the nation invaded Ukraine shortly after the Beijing Olympics.

items.title: Senators’ Cousins out at least one week after hit from Capitals’ Chychrun
items.body: Nick Cousins won't be back on the ice for the next little while. The Ottawa Senators enforcer is out at least one week after absorbing a massive hit from Washington Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun on Tuesday, head coach Travis Green told reporters Wednesday. Cousins was briefly knocked out by the play, Green said. No penalty was called. Washington went on to win 3-2 in overtime. As Cousins looked to clear the puck out of the defensive end late in the third period, Chychrun caught him with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face-down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He did not return. "He's not doing great," Green said after the game, adding that Cousins did not go to the hospital. "I thought it was a head shot to a player who wasn't ready for it. They must have saw it different." The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined there was no penalty. "I should be careful what I say; I don't like seeing that stuff," Senators forward Ridly Greig said. Added captain Thomas Chabot: "I hate, I think everybody hates, these scenes in hockey, in any sport." Cousins, 33, has two goals and one assist in 19 games this season. The Senators are back in action Thursday at home against the Colorado Avalanche.

items.title: Report: GM Briere says Flyers have ‘no plan’ to trade Matvei Michkov
items.summary: ESPN’s Kevin Weekes reported Tuesday that Michkov would be interested in a new start away from the Flyers.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Shockwaves were sent through the hockey universe on Tuesday afternoon when ESPN NHL insider Kevin Weekes reported that Philadelphia Flyers winger Matvei Michkov would be interested in “ a new start ” in the form of a trade to another team. Subsequent reports from multiple insiders, including ESPN’s Emily Kaplan, indicated that if Michkov did indeed want a trade, his camp had not lodged that request directly with the Flyers’ management staff. Now, according to Sportsnet NHL insider Frank Seravalli , Flyers general manager Daniel Briere has no plans to trade Michkov to another team. “This is all news to me… We’ve never discussed that.” Briere told Seravalli. “He’s got so much ahead of him that we’re all really excited about. He’s going in the right direction and it’s exciting to see what he can do already.” Michkov, who is in the final season of his entry-level contract after making the jump to North America beginning in the 2024-25 season, drew the ire of head coach Rick Tocchet last season for showing up to training camp in less than ideal shape. His conditioning was called into question by Tocchet, who scaled back his role from 16:41 of average time on ice as a rookie to 14:50 last season. items.body: Saw Carolina play as a 13-year-old, now facing Kraken in Global Series HELSINKI -- Sebastian Aho is living a dream that took shape 16 years ago. He was 13 years old and found himself at Hartwall Arena -- the mecca of Finnish hockey and home to the Finnish national ice hockey team -- to watch the Carolina Hurricanes take on the Minnesota Wild in the 2010 NHL Premiere Series. The trip from his home in Oulu to the Finnish capital is about seven hours by car, but for Aho it may as well have been a different world. He sat in the stands wide-eyed and imagined himself in the NHL, imagined one day being like the Finnish NHL players in the game below -- Mikko Koivu and Antti Miettinen from the Wild and Jussi Jokinen , Joni Pitkanen , and Tuomo Ruutu from the Hurricanes. When the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland takes place on Thursday, Aho will stand on that same ice, in what is now called Veikkaus Arena, as one of the faces of the Hurricanes, who are the defending Stanley Cup champion. items.title: Briere says Flyers have no plan to trade Michkov
items.summary: The message from Daniel Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Matvei Michkov.
items.body: TORONTO — Despite a report about Matvei Michkov’s apparent unhappiness and potential interest in a change of scenery, the Philadelphia Flyers say they have not received a request for a trade from Michkov’s agent and were surprised by the news. “This is all news to me,” Flyers general manager Daniel Briere said. Beyond that, the message from Briere was clear: The Flyers have no intention of moving Michkov. “No, that’s not the plan at all,” Briere said. “We’ve never discussed that.” The report from NHL Network ’s Kevin Weekes cited “internal turmoil” with the Flyers as part of Michkov’s interest in “wanting a new start elsewhere,” but earlier on Wednesday following the GM Meetings in downtown Toronto, Briere took zero issue with Michkov’s emotion that spilled over to the bench during an in-game confrontation with teammate Nick Seeler. “I actually like the fact that our guys are fiery and they want to win,” Briere said. “That’s what I saw [in Vancouver]. It’s showing competitive players. That’s what we’re looking for, that’s what we want. The reality is, the team hasn’t performed great this year and players expect more out of themselves.” Briere scoffed at the notion that the in-game quarrelling over a sequence in the offensive zone had any indication that the Flyers were lacking in the culture department, as some observers have suggested. “If we had a culture where guys are yelling at each other and no one is responding, a culture that guys don’t care about winning, then we’d be in trouble,” Briere said. “But when you show a culture that guys want to better themselves and they’re not happy where they are, I expect that.” One of the most emotional and competitive players on the last great Flyers teams, Briere said he was glad there weren’t as many cameras as there are now.

No single issue caused this downfall; it was a series of bad trades, poor development, and aggressive management decisions. The amazing thing for Los Angeles is that they were primed to build a sustainable contender around Byfield and Brandt Clarke , but now find themselves in a position where the playoffs feel like a long shot and their contention window is nearly closed. items.body: TORONTO -- All is quiet between the Minnesota Wild and Quinn Hughes , and the team could keep the defenseman past the NHL Trade Deadline on March 1 if he doesn’t sign a new deal, general manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday. Hughes, whom the Wild acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a trade Dec. 12, 2025, is in the final season of a six-year, $47.1 million contract ($7.85 million average annual value) he signed with Vancouver on Oct. 3, 2021. The 27-year-old has been eligible to sign a new contract with the Wild since July 1. If he doesn’t sign before June 30, he will become an unrestricted free agent the next day. On Oct. 24, Hughes said he “wouldn’t be surprised if something happens soon.” But Tuesday, Guerin said the situation is “status quo.” “Because, honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” Would Guerin be willing to keep Hughes past the trade deadline? Hughes won the Norris Trophy as the NHL’s best defenseman in 2024. Since the trade, Hughes has 80 points (11 goals, 69 assists) in 68 games, second on the Wild and second among NHL defensemen. In that span, forward Kirill Kaprizov leads Minnesota with 87 points (44 goals, 43 assists) in 67 games, and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers is first among NHL defensemen with 98 points (26 goals, 72 assists) in 70 games. The Wild (13-3-4), who extended their point streak to nine games (7-0-2) with a 2-1 overtime win at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday, lead the Central Division. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin said. “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.”

items.body: Former Devils forward Dawson Mercer and Kyle Connor each scored twice to lead the Winnipeg Jets to an emotional 4-2 victory over New Jersey on Tuesday. The victory extended Winnipeg's win streak to four games, and halted New Jersey’s at five games. Former Devils netminder Nico Daws made 19 saves for Winnipeg (8-8-3) before a capacity crowd of 15,321 fans at Canada Life Centre. After Mercer gave the Jets a 3-2 lead on the power play at 11:58 of the third period, Connor sealed the outcome with an unassisted empty-net goal. The Devils, who trailed 2-0 after the first period, tied the game in the second period with a pair of goals 44 seconds apart. Bratt scored at 1:14 on a perfect setup from Arseny Gritsyuk from behind the net. Jack Hughes also assisted to extend his point streak to six games. Glass then tied the game at 1:58 when he deflected Jonathan Kovacevic’s shot past Daws. Declan Chisholm also assisted. Connor scored during a two-man advantage at 15:06 of the first period when he deflected Cole Perfetti’s pass past Allen. Mark Scheifele also assisted, moving him into a second-place tie with Dale Hawerchuk in all-time assists in franchise history with 550. Mercer opened the scoring at 7:54 when his snap shot from the faceoff circle beat Allen. items.body: Devils goalie reiterates love for Winnipeg, but some things ‘crossed the line’ WINNIPEG -- Connor Hellebuyck said his family’s safety and uncertainly about his career played a part in requesting a trade from the Winnipeg Jets at the end of last season. But the New Jersey Devils goalie would not point to one thing that made him decide to ask out. “There’s no one singular moment that wasn’t important in all of this decision-making and this is over a span of time,” Hellebuyck said in his return to Canada Life Centre on Tuesday. “I will say with all the uncertainty I was experiencing, there was some moments and some things that happened to my family that for me crossed the line. And as a husband and a father, I felt made that decision very certain, that I needed to be a good husband and a good father and do what’s best for my family and my career.” Hellebuyck, who was traded by the Jets to the Devils on Oct. 23, was addressing the Winnipeg media for the first time since his exit interview April 17, after the Jets failed to qualify for the Stanley Cup Playoffs. items.title: Senators’ Cousins exits after big hit from Capitals’ Chychrun
items.body: The Ottawa Senators went down a forward late in Tuesday's game against the Washington Capitals . Nick Cousins was forced to exit the game after he was on the receiving end of a massive hit from Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun with three minutes remaining in the third period. As Cousins was looking to clear the puck out of the defensive end, Chychrun caught the Senators forward with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He would not return for the remainder of the game. "He's not doing great," head coach Travis Green said after the game . The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined that there was no penalty on the hit.

items.body: Fresh off Hockey Hall of Fame initiation, former Canadiens goalie honored in front of home crowd MIN@MTL: Price gets ovations on joining Canadiens' Ring of Honor It took four minutes for the fans at the Bell Centre to get back in their seats after Carey Price took the ice. The former Montreal Canadiens goaltender – and now a member of the 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame class – was honored on Tuesday at the arena he called home for his entire 15-year NHL career. L'ovation debout de quatre minutes la plus méritée de l'histoire The most well-deserved four-minute standing ovation #GoHabsGo | @CP0031 pic.twitter.com/ehAzCiXF0Z Tuesday’s addition to the Canadiens’ Ring of Honour comes a day after Price’s induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday in Toronto. Price – the Canadiens’ all-time winningest goalie – was drafted by Montreal in the first round of the 2005 NHL Draft, making his debut with the team in the 2007 season. He played his entire career with the Canadiens until his retirement in 2022. He finished his career with a 361-261-79 record and a .917 save percentage with 49 shutouts. In his career-defining 2014-15 season, Price swept the individual NHL awards, winning the William M. Jennings Trophy, Vezina Trophy, Ted Lindsay Award and the Hart Memorial Trophy. He added the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy in the 2021-22 season.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Heinen, Hanifin, Marchment, Panthers By Bradley Keith | at November 10, 2026 7:54 pm According to Aaron Portzline of The Athletic , Columbus forward Danton Heinen did not “immediately” report to AHL Cleveland last week after he cleared waivers . The veteran is reportedly weighing his options while the Blue Jackets organization is giving him the time needed to figure out next steps in his career. Coming up on a decade since his 47-point debut campaign in Boston, the 31-year-old has become more of a rotational depth forward at this point in his career and no longer the strong third line two-way winger he once was. Still, it’s not hard to see why Heinen would want to assess where his career goes next. The 2014 fourth-round pick (Boston) has skated in just 17 AHL games since the 2016-17 season as a prospect. A 12-game stint with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins last season proved he still had more in the tank, dominating with 17 points in 12 games. Heinen accepted a two-way deal to stick around in Ohio for the season, making the team but coming away scoreless in his 10 games, averaging 10:10 a night, the lowest usage of his 11-year career. Currently 26th in the AHL the Monsters already have a roster full of veterans including Steven Lorentz , who has lit it up with seven goals in nine games, as well as Carson Soucy who just joined the club. Whatever happens ahead, Columbus respectfully is making sure they do right of the British Columbia native who has skated in 622 NHL games in his career.

Terry, 29, has missed the Ducks’ first 18 games of the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from summer hip surgery. Ducks head coach Joel Quenneville said Tuesday that Terry is “likely” to play as the Ducks welcome the Predators to the Honda Center on Wednesday. In 61 games with the Ducks during the 2025-26 regular season, Terry collected 19 goals and 57 points. The Denver product added three goals and 11 points in 12 playoff contests as the Ducks defeated the Edmonton Oilers in the first round before being eliminated by the Vegas Golden Knights . A four-time 20-goal scorer, Terry has consistently been one of the Ducks’ most dangerous offensive players since establishing himself as an NHL regular in the 2020-21 season. In his absence, the Ducks have gotten off to a 10-7-1 start to the 2026-27 season, posting a plus-3 goal differential. The Ducks originally selected Terry in the fifth round (No. 148 overall) of the 2015 NHL Draft. The 6’0″ right wing spent his first three post-draft seasons playing close to home at the University of Denver, suiting up for Team USA along the way at both the 2017 World Juniors and the 2018 Winter Olympics. Terry signed with the Ducks in 2018 and gradually developed into a top-six scoring forward for the club, topping out with 37 goals and 67 points in 75 games during the 2021-22 season. items.summary: In Connor Hellebuyck’s careful attempt to prevent this from becoming a sticky situation, he has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known.
items.body: WINNIPEG — In his much-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday, Connor Hellebuyck desperately tried to keep his story straight. But in his careful attempt to prevent his departure from Winnipeg from becoming a sticky situation, the former franchise goaltender has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known. Sitting in front of dozens of reporters at Canada Life Centre, Hellebuyck looked and acted like a man wanting to have his cake and eat it, too. Rather than speak clearly and concisely about the treatment he received from disappointed Canadians and a clear desire to move his family south of the border, Hellebuyck opted to dance around the subject. Only adding insult to injury, Hellebuyck won't even face the music Tuesday against his former team. Despite his insistence that he felt a "duty" to play, New Jersey Devils general manager Sunny Mehta stepped in with a dizzying analytics-led excuse. Citing a "reduction in our expected win probability," Mehta is sitting his all-star goalie. The irony of Hellebuyck demanding out of Winnipeg, where he had full control of his playing time, to join an organization that now dictates his ice time through analytics is too difficult to ignore. But to understand just how brazen it was for Hellebuyck to sit at a table inside Canada Life Centre and ask fans to separate his exit from his legacy, you have to look at how that exit played out. "The day I said I was a Jet for life, I meant it," Hellebuyck said. "But I also didn't foresee the future that was going to happen." items.body: TORONTO — Remember a few weeks ago when Buffalo’s Owen Power was incensed that he was wrongly whistled for a high-sticking penalty? It was friendly fire. Power didn’t high-stick Matvei Michkov, who was done dirty by his own teammate, Trevor Zegras. All 18,000 fans in KeyBank Arena in Buffalo saw it on replay. The NHL’s Situation Room saw it in near real time. But once the call is made on the ice, according to current rules, there’s no chance to review it and it cannot be rescinded. “The only four people that don’t get to see it are the four guys in striped shirts,” NHL senior executive vice president of hockey operations Colin Campbell said. “There’s times we would like to get involved.” To that end, Campbell said the NHL will explore in the coming months how things like rapid replay assist technology can aid on-ice officials. Think something that wouldn’t involve a long huddle or review, but how quickly, as in the NFL, the spot of the ball is corrected, or how fast it is relayed to the officiating team that a runner stepped out of bounds. “The game’s not perfect,” Campbell said. “How can we help them out? “You look at football, what they’ve done with the quarterback’s helmet. You look at baseball, with the pitcher and catcher (pitchcom device). All sports are expanding communication.” The discussion was brought to the NHL’s 32 general managers in their meeting on Tuesday and Campbell said the “appetite was good.” Rule changes cannot be enacted mid-season but can be voted on in Florida in March for the Competition Committee to implement for 2027-28. items.title: NHL, NHLPA to discuss possibility of ‘smoothing’ salary cap over next two seasons
items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap will be $113.5 million next season, and is projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The NHL’s salary cap has increased substantially over the last couple of seasons, leading to some monstrous contracts getting handed out this past offseason. It’s expected to continue to skyrocket in the years to come. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , however, the league is looking at the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap’s growth over the next two seasons. At Tuesday’s GM meetings, it was decided that the NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss ways of making the salary cap’s increases over the next couple seasons less dramatic year over year, with the hopes of creating a more stable salary environment across the league. The NHL’s salary cap this season is $104 million, which increased from $95.5 million last season and $88 million the season prior. It will grow to $113.5 million next season, and is currently projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season. According to Friedman, one strategy the league could pursue is raising next season’s cap from $113.5 million by a certain amount, and then lowering the 2028-29 cap by the same amount, thereby shrinking the cap spike between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. For example, if next year’s cap is raised from $113.5 to $115.5 million, representing a $2 million bump, then the cap for the 2028-29 season would be decreased by $2 million, going from a projected $127.5 million to a projected $125.5 million. This would keep the difference between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 salary caps to $10 million. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the NHL’s salary cap stayed flat at $81.5 million for three seasons, from 2019-20 through 2021-22. items.title: Canucks quarter-mark report: Few bright spots in dark days of rebuild
items.summary: There has been no joy for the Canucks so far. And on several nights, some essential pride has been missing too, as Vancouver crashed to its worst opening quarter in franchise history.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Losing hockey games is not the same thing as playing losing hockey. Coach Manny Malhotra warned everyone about this ahead of the first full season of the Vancouver Canucks ’ rebuild. “There’s a very big difference between losing games, which is inevitable. . . and playing losing hockey,” Malhotra told reporters on the eve of training camp in September. “The measure of our group will be on playing the right way, doing the things that we’re talking about, having details to your game, which is going to give us an opportunity to win. That’s where the pride or the joy will come from: knowing that we are learning, we’re doing the things that we’re asked, and it’s getting better.” There has been no joy for the Canucks so far. What’s worse, on several nights, some of that essential pride has been missing, too, as Vancouver crashed to its worst opening quarter in franchise history. Even as the Canucks were losing 16 out of 17 games, they appeared to be making some progress in their structure and details, and willingness and ability to compete. Their 3-16-1 record, which included a 2-1 start to the season, equals the worst 20-game winning percentage (.175) by any NHL team since the salary-cap era began in 2005. items.title: Wild activate Jared Spurgeon off injured reserve
items.summary: Minnesota has also assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to the AHL’s Iowa Wild.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are welcoming their captain back into the fold. On Tuesday, the Wild announced that they have activated defenseman Jared Spurgeon off of injured reserve. In a corresponding move, the Wild have assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Iowa Wild. Spurgeon, 36, has missed Minnesota’s last five games , and was also out for a four-game stretch with an upper-body injury earlier this season. In 10 games played so far, the Edmonton native has a goal and four assists for five points while averaging about 20 and a half minutes of ice time. Last season, Spurgeon notched six goals and 16 assists for 22 points in 79 games while averaging about 19 and a half minutes of ice time. He then put up no goals and an assist while averaging a tick over 21 minutes in 11 playoff games. Selected by the New York Islanders in the sixth round of the 2008 NHL Entry Draft, Spurgeon did not sign his entry-level deal with New York and instead signed with Minnesota after his five-year junior career with the Spokane Chiefs of the Western Hockey League (WHL). Spurgeon is now in his 17th NHL season, all with the Wild. He ranks second in games played on Minnesota’s all-time list with 1,022, just six games back of Mikko Koivu. He also ranks third on the Wild’s all-time scoring list with 443 points. He is in the final season of a seven-year, $53.03 million contract . Pitlick, 35, has gone scoreless in 12 games played for Minnesota this season. The Minneapolis, Minnesota native has played for nine different teams over parts of 12 seasons in the NHL. Minnesota kicks off a three-game road trip against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday before visiting the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday.

The NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap over the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. Under the current three-year agreement — which concludes at the end of next season — the salary cap for 2027-28 will be $113.5 million. At September’s Board of Governors meeting in New York City, the league provided a preliminary estimate of $127.5 million for 2028-29. What the league and players’ association could agree to is raising next season’s ceiling and lowering the 2028-29 number by the same amount. For example, if they decided to raise 2027-28 by $2 million to $115.5 million, they would drop the following year to $125.5 million. Again, there is nothing concrete at this time, just a willingness to discuss the issue over the next few months. The NBA went through something similar after a major television contract jumped its cap from $70 million in 2015-16 to $94 million in 2016-17. After it was decided that summer created too much carnage, the latest CBA prevents any jump being larger than 10 per cent. We’ll see what the NHL and NHLPA come up with, if both agree on a change.

items.body: Register Login Canucks Make Multiple Roster Moves By Brennan McClain | at November 10, 2026 1:30 pm The Vancouver Canucks are shaking up their defensive corps. According to a team announcement , the Canucks have claimed defenseman Cameron Crotty from the Minnesota Wild. In a corresponding roster move, Vancouver has assigned defenseman Victor Mancini to the AHL’s Abbotsford Canucks. Crotty, 27, will play for his third team in under two weeks. The Ottawa, ON, native began his season with the Ottawa Senators after joining his hometown team as an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2025-26 campaign. Because of Artem Zub ’s injury in last spring’s postseason, Crotty made Ottawa’s opening-night roster. Although he was originally a depth defender, Crotty got the chance to play for the Sens after they ran into more injury concerns on their blue line. The Boston University alumnus went scoreless in three games with a +1 rating, averaging 11:09 of ice time per game. As they returned to health, Ottawa placed Crotty on waivers on October 28th, and he was claimed by the Wild the following day. Similarly, Minnesota used Crotty as a depth defender as they awaited the return of Brock Faber and Jared Spurgeon . Assuming one of the two returns tonight, the Wild were willing to risk losing Crotty on waivers to create room for Faber or Spurgeon. Meanwhile, Mancini returns to AHL Abbotsford after going scoreless in eight games for Vancouver. The Hancock, MI, native is in his third year with the Canucks after they acquired him from the New York Rangers in the J.T. Miller trade. Unfortunately, he hasn’t yet turned into the defenseman that the Canucks believe he can be. Although he’s only 24, Mancini will need to turn things around soon if he wants any staying power on Vancouver’s blue line.

items.summary: Marchment was given a pair of minor penalties for roughing on the play on Monday night.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images A notable grinder is paying up for his recent actions. On Tuesday, the NHL Department of Player Safety announced that San Jose Sharks forward Mason Marchment has been fined $5,000 for roughing New York Islanders forward Victor Eklund. The incident in question came a little before the halfway mark of the third period. Eklund threw a hard hit to Sharks winger Kiefer Sherwood along the boards. Marchment, none too pleased with the check, came over to his teammate’s defense. Marchment gave a couple of hard shoves to Eklund before dropping the gloves as a melee ensued. While Eklund was caught up in the kerfuffle, Marchment gave a couple of hard rights to a rather defenseless Eklund. Marchment received the only penalties on the play, as he was handed two minor penalties for roughing. Marchment, who ended the night with six penalty minutes, got the last laugh with his team, as San Jose picked up a 3-2 shootout victory. The 31-year-old missed on his attempt in the fifth round of the skills competition. The fine is the maximum allowable amount under the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement. The money goes directly to theNHL Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. This isn’t the first time Marchment has faced supplemental discipline in his NHL career. In February 2024, then with the Florida Panthers, he was fined $5,000 for interference against Toronto Maple Leafs defenseman Jack McCabe. In 20 games this season, Marchment has scored four goals and three assists for seven points, sitting tied for fourth on the team in goals. Eklund has posted six goals and nine points in 17 games thus far, good for second and fifth on the Islanders, respectively.

items.body: Connor Hellebuyck is giving a bit of insight in his decision to request a trade from the Winnipeg Jets . Returning to Winnipeg for the first time since being traded on Oct. 23, the New Jersey Devils goaltender said incidents with his family played a significant role in his decision. "There's no one singular moment that wasn't important in all of this decision making, and this is over a span of time," Hellebuyck told reporters in Winnipeg on Tuesday. The 33-year-old has three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy as league MVP under his belt, all won as a member of the Jets. He backstopped the United States to Olympic gold — their first in four decades — at the 2026 Winter Olympics. When asked if that Olympic gold, which was earned against Canada, played a role in his decision to request a trade out of a Canadian market, he ceded that there are difficulties present as an American playing north of the border. The right-handed rearguard had been on a conditioning assignment with the Blues’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Springfield Thunderbirds, but didn’t appear in any games before being recalled last Friday. Mailloux had been on the shelf since September, when he injured his right hand during a preseason fight with Chicago Blackhawks forward Cole Smith in St. Louis’ final game of the preseason. The 23-year-old was placed on IR after undergoing surgery. The Belle River, Ont. native entered the 2026-27 campaign looking to build on his first full season in the NHL. In 67 games with the Blues last year, he scored five goals and eight assists for 13 points, registering a plus/minus of -10 while averaging 16:46 of ice time. Mailloux is expected to be a key part of the Blues’ blue line for a long time, which is why the team acquired him from the Montreal Canadiens via trade in July 2025. In 75 career games in the NHL, Mailloux has posted seven goals and 11 assists for 18 points. The Blues (7-8-2) are struggling to keep pace in the Western Conference Wild Card race. items.title: Report: NHL GMs ‘warm’ to idea of video-assisted review for officials
items.summary: Plays in question would help refs get the call right on penalties they might’ve missed or mistakenly called.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Christopher Trim-Imagn Images If there hasn’t been enough video review in the game today, just wait. According to insider Frank Seravalli, NHL executive vice president and director of hockey operations Colin Campbell stated that, during a meeting among the league’s general managers on Tuesday, a discussion of video-assisted review took place. The idea is that there will be direct communication to on-ice officials to amend penalties, most notably friendly-fire high-sticking. Per Seravalli, Campbell said reception from the GMs was “warm.” There is a potential vote coming up in March, with any rule changes being implemented for the 2027-28 season. Any potential rule change would also have to be approved by the NHL Players’ Association. According to responses on social media, fans seem to be in favor of the idea of righting any wrongs by referees. The one concern would be what the video review process would be like and, more or less, how long it would take. These days, if there is a call that officials feel like they messed up on, the second ref would come over to discuss the play before making a decision to reverse the call. If there were VAR put in place for penalties, many around the game hope that it can be a quick fix, rather than a long, drawn-out review that we sometimes see for potential offsides or goalie interference penalties. There certainly would be positives in helping out the refs, who can sometimes miss infractions in real time, especially with how fast the game is played these days.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images The Detroit Red Wings are welcoming a couple of forwards back into their lineup. On Tuesday, the Red Wings announced that they have activated center Marco Kasper and winger Mason Appleton off of injured reserve. Kasper, 22, has been out since Detroit’s season-opening 2-0 loss to the New York Rangers with an upper-body injury. Last season, the Austrian national notched nine goals and 10 assists for 19 points in 81 games. Selected eighth overall by the Red Wings in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft, Kasper spent the 2022-23 season playing mostly for Rögle BK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL), where he had eight goals and 15 assists for 23 points in 52 games. He also made his NHL debut that season, going scoreless in one game for Detroit. Kasper came to North America full-time for the 2023-24 season, in which he registered 14 goals and 21 assists for 35 points in 71 games for the Red Wings’ American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Grand Rapids Griffins. His rookie NHL season came in 2024-25, when he put up 19 goals and 18 assists for a career-best 37 points in 77 games. Appleton, 30, went scoreless over Detroit’s first two games this season, but has been out since with an undisclosed injury. Last season, the Green Bay, Wisconsin native had six goals and eight assists for 14 points in 65 games for the Red Wings. Selected by the Winnipeg Jets in the sixth round of the 2015 NHL Draft, Appleton spent seven of his first eight NHL seasons with the Jets, playing just one season for the Seattle Kraken in 2021-22, before signing a two-year, $5.8 million contract with Detroit in July of 2025. items.title: The story behind Jake Middleton’s tribute to his grandfather’s wartime sacrifice
items.summary: Jake Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. The Flames defenceman’s grandfather served in the Second World War, and Middleton shares his love with a deeply meaningful tattoo sleeve.
items.body: CALGARY — The poppy fell from his father's chest and into the grave. Jake Middleton was seven years old, standing among family and friends near the military base in Wainwright, Alta., watching as they lowered his grandfather, Robert Bruce, into the ground. Somewhere in the emotion of that moment, it came loose and tumbled onto the coffin below. One by one, those gathered for “Papa's” funeral removed their own poppies, stepped forward and tossed them into the grave, sending their final tribute down with the man they had come to say goodbye to. And every Nov. 11, when the trumpets begin to sound, that little boy comes rushing back. "You know, I always get a frog in my throat when those start playing on Remembrance Day," said the Calgary Flames defenceman. It's a memory that has never really left him. Neither has the man who inspired it. Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. His extensive tattoo sleeve is a deeply personal tribute to his grandfather, a Second World War dispatch rider who served in North Africa, France, Germany and England. It's a remarkable piece of work, and Middleton has never been particularly shy about showing it off. Those familiar with his entertaining media availabilities know they’re often delivered shirtless. But there's considerably more to it than ink and impressive artwork. There's a grandson's love for a grandfather he lost too young, a family's military history and an appreciation for sacrifices that become increasingly meaningful with age. items.body: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Too Much Too Soon?: How Jets Rookie Viggo Bjorck Is Handling The Pressures Of The NHL Tony Ferrari Partner Nov 10, 2026 5:20 PM Published Nov 10, 2026 5:20 PM It took Viggo Bjorck 17 games to hit the scoresheet for the first time in his NHL career. While offense is just one dimension of what makes the 18-year-old such a special prospect, how has he handled his role with the Winnipeg Jets early on? Heading into the 2026 NHL draft, it felt like everyone knew who the first two picks would be, and what level they'd end up playing at this season. Gavin McKenna and Ivar Stenberg seemed destined to immediately be in the NHL, and as with most years, the expectation for other players in the class decreased. That said, when Viggo Bjorck made the Winnipeg Jets out of camp after being selected eighth overall, it didn't shock anyone. items.title: Wild could keep unsigned Quinn Hughes past trade deadline, GM says
items.body: The Minnesota Wild are going all-in on their Stanley Cup aspirations this season, even if it means losing their star defenceman to free agency. General manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday that the team might opt to keep Quinn Hughes past the trade deadline even if he does not re-sign with the Wild, running the risk of losing the one-time Norris Trophy winner for nothing. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin told reporters in Toronto, per NHL.com . “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.” When asked if that would extend to keeping an unsigned Hughes past the trade deadline, Guerin said yes. Hughes, in the final year of a six-year, $47.1-million contract, became eligible to re-sign with the Wild on July 1. On that front, Guerin said progress towards a deal remains "status quo." "Honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” The Wild acquired Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks in December 2025 in exchange for Zeev Buium, Liam Ohgren, Marco Rossi and a 2026 first-round pick.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images It’s official: a former NHL sniper is heading overseas. On Tuesday, the Kontinental Hockey League announced that former NHL winger Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with HC Sibir Novosibirsk. Kane signs with Sibir, even though multiple reports stated that he was receiving offers from teams on this side of the Atlantic. His agent, Dan Milstein, stated that Kane would be heading to the KHL during last week’s episode of DFO Rundown . The 35-year-old moves to Russia after spending the 2025-26 season with the Vancouver Canucks . On a team that finished with the worst record in the NHL, Kane managed to score 13 goals and 18 assists for 31 points, finishing sixth on the team in scoring, while appearing in 71 games. It came after a rather successful four seasons with the Edmonton Oilers , where Kane’s physical play and scoring touch helped his team reach the Western Conference Finals three times, advancing to the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025. In 1,001 regular-season games, which included stops with the Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks and Winnipeg Jets (formerly the Atlanta Thrashers), Kane potted 339 goals and 309 assists for 648 pints, with another 55 points in 97 postseason contests. This won’t be the first time Kane has played in Russia. During the lockout that canceled half of the 2012-13 season, he signed with Dynamo Minsk, scoring two points in 12 games. Sibir is 8-1-4-13 so far this season, sitting with the worst record in the KHL’s Eastern Conference and 20th in the league’s overall standings. items.body: Register Login Evander Kane Signs With KHL’s Sibir Novosibirsk By Brennan McClain | at November 10, 2026 7:45 am The former fourth-overall pick of the 2009 NHL Draft is taking his talents overseas. According to the KHL , Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with Sibir Novosibirsk in the KHL. Earlier in November, in speaking to David Pagnotta on DFO Insider , Dan Milstein of Gold Star Hockey confirmed that Evander Kane would sign with a KHL organization and that a formal announcement should be expected in the next few days; the team has officially come to light. Because of his age and poor play during last season with the Vancouver Canucks, Milstein’s announcement strongly suggests that Kane won’t return to the NHL. Although there were plenty of ups and downs, few players get to enjoy a 16-year career like Kane did. That career began on June 26, 2009, when the Atlanta Thrashers selected Kane with the fourth overall pick in the 2009 NHL Draft. He immediately jumped to the NHL, scoring 14 goals and 26 points in 66 games, good for a ninth-place finish in Calder Trophy voting. Kane spent one more season with the Thrashers and remained with the team when they relocated, becoming the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets. His first season in Winnipeg is arguably his career-best campaign. The Vancouver, BC, native finished second on the team in scoring behind Blake Wheeler , registering 30 goals and 57 points in 74 games with a +11 rating. A few weeks before the 2012-13 campaign was supposed to start, the Jets signed Kane to a six-year, $31.5MM ($5.25MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, Kane’s relationship with the Jets rapidly began to sour. Toward the end of the 2013-14 campaign, Kane was accused of assault in his hometown and was subsequently sued for financial damages.

items.body: VANCOUVER – It seems especially cruel — but typical — that what sure looks like the worst season in Vancouver Canucks ’ history will be extended by two games by the National Hockey League and its players’ association. On the other hand, an 84-game season, divided by four, means the Canucks have one more game to avoid manufacturing the NHL’s worst opening quarter since the salary-cap era began in 2005. So, despite an array of gruesome numbers surrounding the Canucks, arithmetic may still be their friend. They could use one. items.title: Stenberg leads Sharks past Islanders in shootout to stop 5-game skid
items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak. Tyler Toffoli had a goal and an assist, and Stenberg also scored in regulation for the Sharks (8-11-1). Stenberg has six goals and is tied for the scoring lead among NHL rookies. Ben Hutton and Victor Eklund scored for the Islanders (7-6-4), who have lost four straight games (0-2-2). Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 shots. Stenberg put the Sharks on the board late in the first period after Toffoli sent a shot toward the net. Stenberg got a piece of the puck to redirect it past Sorokin and tie the game at 1. San Jose again rallied from a goal down midway through the second when Toffoli’s shot deflected off Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech and into the net. It was Toffoli’s first goal in eight games. Hutton opened the scoring early in the first after Simon Holmstrom’s pass found him with an open look. Eklund put New York ahead 2-1 early in the second with a power-play goal. Sharks center Alexander Wennberg, who returned after missing 10 games, was called for the penalty that led to the power play. The game got chippy late in the second as fights broke out, leading to four five-minute major penalties. Barclay Goodrow received a penalty for fighting Mitchell Chaffee, and Ty Dellandrea was penalized for fighting Kyle MacLean.
